title: From pan-life phase insights to PhaseHub: Analyzing protein condensate complexity.
authors: Liang, Qiyu; Gao, Weibo; Miao, Yansong
one_liner_zh: 该文跨物种分析相分离蛋白并开发PhaseHub数据库，整合序列特征与互作网络预测凝聚体枢纽，虽以无序蛋白/相分离为对象且涉及PPI，但方法偏生物信息学分析而非AI/物理模拟建模，机制深度有限。
abstract: Intracellular biomolecular condensation forms multicomponent signaling hubs that regulate development, stress responses, and environmental adaptation. While the molecular grammar encoded within scaffold proteins defines the basal associative features driving condensation, heterotypic condensates are intrinsically dynamic, multicomponent, and far-from-equilibrium systems. Consequently, how condensates organize component composition, stoichiometry, and functional specificity in space and time under physiological conditions remains poorly understood. Addressing this challenge requires integrative frameworks that combine predictive biophysical features with experimental information on protein abundance, interaction networks, subcellular localization, and evolutionary conservation. In this study, we first analyzed phase separation (PS) proteins across the tree of life in 1106 species, revealing a stark contrast in computationally predicted PS propensity between eukaryotes and prokaryotes, with genome size as a key determinant. Through a broad analysis of amino acid homorepeat-containing proteins (HRPs) across all species, we uncovered how PS evolves via a balance between functional condensation and avoidance of harmful, aggregation-prone sequences. We further identified potential signaling hubs and components across kingdoms by integrating PS-positive proteins with experimentally derived abundance and interactome data from four model eukaryotic species. Using Arabidopsis as a model, we dissected the relationships among PS propensity, condensation hub prediction, HRPs, subcellular localization, and structural conservation. Finally, we developed PhaseHub, a user-friendly interface for exploring scaffold-client dynamics, PS components, sequence signatures within each PS protein, and hubs. Collectively, our work provides an evolutionary framework for understanding multicomponent PS hubs by integrating molecular grammar with physiological context, thereby facilitating hypothesis generation and rational design.
abstract_zh: 细胞内生物分子凝聚形成多组分信号枢纽，调控发育、应激反应和环境适应。尽管支架蛋白内编码的分子语法定义了驱动凝聚的基础关联特征，异型凝聚体本质上是动态、多组分且远离平衡态的系统。因此，在生理条件下，凝聚体如何组织组分构成、化学计量比以及时空功能特异性仍知之甚少。应对这一挑战需要整合框架，将预测性生物物理特征与蛋白质丰度、相互作用网络、亚细胞定位和进化保守性的实验信息相结合。在本研究中，我们首先分析了1106个物种生命树中的相分离 (phase separation) 蛋白，揭示了真核生物与原核生物之间计算预测的相分离倾向的显著差异，其中基因组大小是关键决定因素。通过对所有物种中含氨基酸同聚重复蛋白 (homorepeat-containing proteins) 的广泛分析，我们揭示了相分离如何通过功能性凝聚与避免有害、易聚集序列之间的平衡而进化。我们进一步通过将相分离阳性蛋白与四种模式真核物种的实验衍生丰度和相互作用组数据整合，鉴定了跨界的潜在信号枢纽和组分。以拟南芥为模型，我们剖析了相分离倾向、凝聚枢纽预测、同聚重复蛋白、亚细胞定位和结构保守性之间的关系。最后，我们开发了PhaseHub，一个用户友好的界面，用于探索支架-客户动态、相分离组分、每个相分离蛋白内的序列特征以及枢纽。总体而言，我们的工作通过将分子语法与生理背景整合，为理解多组分相分离枢纽提供了进化框架，从而促进假设生成和理性设计。
